title: Knee joint aspiration

guidelineVersions: SANJO 2023 (European guideline; local UK procedural policy also required)

brief.scenario: You are a core surgical trainee in the acute assessment area. A 62-year-old has a painful swollen native right knee for two days, cannot bear weight and is haemodynamically stable. The temperature is 38.1°C. A manikin is supplied. No prior joint replacement.
brief.task: Explain and demonstrate diagnostic knee aspiration on the model and outline specimen handling and initial treatment. You have 9 minutes.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: potential septic arthritis: diagnose promptly while protecting the joint and avoiding a contaminated tap.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: calling a hot knee “gout” before sampling, or using crystals to rule out infection.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: recognise urgency, check sepsis and obtain consent.

flow: Assess stability, suspected infection and relevant history.
Describe and demonstrate the model aspiration safely.
Escalate, organise definitive care and safety-net.

grid.label: Recognise septic arthritis
grid.fail: Labels hot knee gout and plans outpatient review.
grid.pass: Recognises septic arthritis as a priority differential.
grid.high: States normal CRP or crystal finding cannot exclude it.

grid.label: Assess sepsis and risk
grid.pass: Assesses ABCDE, observations, immunosuppression, anticoagulants and prosthesis history.
grid.high: Explains that shock changes sampling/antibiotic timing.

grid.label: Explain and consent
grid.borderline: Explains only that fluid will be removed.
grid.pass: Explains indication, discomfort, bleeding, infection and alternatives; consents.
grid.high: Checks patient concerns, allergies and analgesia needs.

grid.label: Position and landmarks
grid.borderline: Names knee but no safe approach.
grid.pass: Positions supported knee, identifies effusion and suitable insertion region on model.
grid.high: Checks proposed trajectory against anatomy and offers ultrasound assistance if uncertain.

grid.label: Asepsis and safety
grid.pass: Hand hygiene, sterile equipment, disinfects and allows skin to dry; avoids cellulitic route where possible.
grid.high: Maintains sterile field and stops/repositions if unsafe.

grid.label: Aspiration technique
grid.pass: Demonstrates careful needle approach and gentle fluid aspiration on model.
grid.high: Recognises dry tap; does not force needle or inject saline just to obtain culture.

grid.label: Samples and priorities
grid.fail: Discards sample or sends only crystals.
grid.borderline: Sends Gram stain but not culture.
grid.pass: Labels urgent culture, cell count/differential and crystals; culture is priority if volume limited.
grid.high: Adds Gram stain and blood cultures when febrile; coordinates with microbiology.

grid.label: Urgent treatment and escalation
grid.fail: Waits for final culture before seeking help.
grid.borderline: Plans review without urgent specialist input.
grid.pass: Escalates to orthopaedics, considers drainage and antibiotics after sampling if stable.
grid.high: Explains immediate sepsis treatment if unstable, without delaying antibiotics.

grid.label: Patient communication and completion
grid.fail: Leaves an open puncture or no explanation.
grid.borderline: Dresses wound but gives no plan.
grid.pass: Withdraws safely, applies dressing, labels samples, documents and explains next steps.
grid.high: Adds analgesia, reassessment plan and clear deterioration advice.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: This seems like gout. I can just remove some fluid tomorrow.

fail.speaker: patient
fail.text: I cannot put any weight on it and I feel hot.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Fever is probably due to the swelling; I do not need observations.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The temperature is 38.1°C, blood pressure 126/74, pulse 94. What will you do?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will put a needle in now; it is quick.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Anywhere around the swollen part should work.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: There is red inflamed skin over your first chosen point.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That should not matter; I can puncture through it.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: A small amount of straw-coloured fluid is obtained.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: If it contains crystals this proves there is no infection, so I will inject steroid into the joint now.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Crystals only. The rest can go in the bin.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will wait for the final culture result before asking orthopaedics or my senior for help.

fail.speaker: patient
fail.text: What if the pain gets worse?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: You can come back another time.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I am the core surgical trainee. A hot swollen knee with fever can represent an infection inside the joint, so I need to assess and investigate it urgently.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It can damage a joint if untreated; aspiration helps identify the cause promptly.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Are you faint, shivery or confused? Do you have a replacement knee, immune-suppressing medicines, allergies or blood-thinning medicines?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: I have no replacement; I am not on blood thinners. I feel feverish, but not faint.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Observations: temperature 38.1°C, pulse 94, BP 126/74 and normal mentation.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: They are stable for urgent sampling, but I would repeat observations and assess for evolving sepsis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I recommend aspirating fluid from the knee. It can be uncomfortable; infection, bleeding and injury are uncommon risks. We will use sterile technique and offer analgesia. Is that acceptable?

pass.speaker: patient
pass.text: Yes. Please explain as you go.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: On the model I position and support the knee, identify the effusion and choose an established safe entry route based on the anatomy. I would use ultrasound assistance if the effusion or landmarks were unclear.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What if the skin over the site is inflamed?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would avoid passing through a skin abscess, and avoid cellulitic skin if another safe approach is possible. After hand hygiene I use sterile equipment, prepare the skin and let antiseptic dry.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I would advance carefully on the model, gently aspirate, and stop to reassess rather than force through resistance.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: You obtain 4 mL of cloudy joint fluid.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I send an urgent sterile specimen for microbiological culture, synovial white count and differential, and crystal analysis. I also request Gram stain. If volume is limited, culture takes priority.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will contact orthopaedics urgently for suspected septic arthritis and discuss antibiotics after aspiration while the patient is stable, using local policy and microbiology advice. Definitive washout may be needed.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not yet. I need a senior review, blood tests and monitoring while we act on the possibility of joint infection. I will cover the site, document what we did and keep you updated.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Good morning, I am the core surgical trainee. Your knee is acutely hot, swollen and extremely painful. Infection in the joint is one of the most important conditions to exclude; fluid sampling is urgent.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Could it just be arthritis?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Inflammation and crystals are possible, but neither the appearance nor even finding crystals reliably rules out infection.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Before proceeding I want a sepsis assessment: current observations, mental state, circulation and any immunosuppression, recent injections, joint operations, skin infection, bleeding medicine or allergies.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: No operation or injections. I take no anticoagulant and have no drug allergy. I feel feverish.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: BP 126/74, pulse 94, temperature 38.1°C. No shock.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: We can prioritise sampling immediately while arranging blood tests and blood cultures because of the fever. If the patient became septic or shocked, antibiotics would not wait for aspiration.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would like to numb and clean the area and draw fluid into a sterile syringe. The principal discomfort is a brief needle pain; we will stop if you want. Bleeding and introducing infection are potential risks. May I continue?

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Yes. I would prefer pain relief.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will arrange suitable analgesia and use local anaesthetic according to local protocol if appropriate.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I expose and support the knee, examine the effusion, identify the accessible approach on the model and ensure my path does not pass through a skin abscess or major structures.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The first proposed site has erythematous overlying skin.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would choose another safe route if feasible, maintain full asepsis and allow the antiseptic to dry fully. I will not traverse an abscess.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I aspirate gently. If I obtain no fluid I reconsider positioning and request ultrasound rather than blindly redirecting repeatedly or injecting saline to generate a sample.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Four millilitres of cloudy fluid obtained.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I prioritise sterile culture, then cell count/differential and crystals, and ask for Gram stain; crystals do not remove the need for cultures. I label knee, side, time and prior antibiotic exposure.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I call orthopaedics for urgent assessment for drainage and discuss empiric antibiotics with microbiology after specimens because the patient is currently stable. I will not wait for a final culture. If physiology deteriorates, treat sepsis immediately.

high.speaker: patient
high.text: Will I lose the use of my knee?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The reason we are acting today is to reduce that risk. I will cover the puncture, reassess pain and observations, document the samples and explain the specialist plan to you.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Summarise your main priority.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A native hot joint is presumed potentially septic until assessed; prompt aseptic aspiration, organism identification and urgent orthopaedic-directed treatment are the priority.

failures.move: Sending suspected septic arthritis home untreated may permit irreversible cartilage injury.
Passing a needle through an overlying abscess introduces infection risk.
Discarding fluid or failing to send culture loses critical diagnosis.
Delaying antibiotics in septic shock for aspiration can be life-threatening.
Injecting steroid before infection is excluded risks worsening active infection.

recovery.when: If you implied crystals exclude infection
recovery.line: I need to correct myself: crystals can coexist with infection, so the sample still needs culture.
If this patient becomes unstable, I will treat sepsis immediately while senior help and sampling are organised.

knowledge.fact: Acute hot swollen joint requires high suspicion for septic arthritis, with or without fever.
Aspiration should occur promptly when native septic arthritis is suspected.
Prioritise bacterial identification, synovial WBC/PMN and crystals; crystals do not rule out sepsis.
Strict antisepsis and avoidance of a subcutaneous abscess are required; do not inject saline to increase culture yield.
Synovial culture in sterile tubes and Gram stain are recommended; febrile patients may need blood cultures.
In stable patients aspiration precedes antibiotics; with sepsis/septic shock antibiotics should not be delayed for sampling.

recall.think: A hot native knee with fever is septic until carefully assessed.
recall.say: “We need a sterile fluid sample today to look for infection.”
do: Consent • check sepsis • sterile model aspiration • culture, count, crystals.

numbers.meaning: No single synovial WBC threshold definitively diagnoses or excludes septic arthritis

recall.trap: Crystals and a low CRP do not rule out septic arthritis.
recall.finish: Orthopaedic escalation, sample handover, treatment plan and reassessment.

sources.name: Ravn C et al. Guideline for management of septic arthritis in native joints (SANJO). Journal of Bone and Joint Infection 8:29–37, 2023
sources.supports: diagnostic approach questions 1–5, microbiological methods questions 7–9, empirical antibiotics question 12. European guideline, not a UK national guideline; used where UK equivalent detail was not confirmed.

partner.opening: Explain and demonstrate diagnostic knee aspiration on the model and outline specimen handling and initial treatment.
partner.actorBrief: Opening patient line: “My knee is very painful and swollen; I can hardly stand.” Only if asked: “I have not had a knee replacement, take no anticoagulant and have no drug allergies.”

reveals.trigger: When requested; if candidate asks about sepsis assessment
reveals.finding: Examiner gives observations when requested; if candidate asks about sepsis assessment, provide stable physiology.

curveballs.safeAnswer: I would avoid passing through a skin abscess, and avoid cellulitic skin if another safe approach is possible. After hand hygiene I use sterile equipment, prepare the skin and let antiseptic dry.

curveballs.prompt: Only after aspiration: 4 mL cloudy fluid. If the candidate has not requested aspiration, do not volunteer the finding.
